image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a wooden bookshelf loudspeaker. The speaker features a curved front baffle with a wood veneer finish. Visible components include a yellowish cone mid-range/woofer driver with a black dust cap and rubber surround, and an angled tweeter module mounted on the top surface. A second driver (likely a woofer) is partially visible at the bottom edge. The background consists of wooden paneling and stacked firewood.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a box-shaped enclosure with a distinct rectangular footprint, although the front corners are rounded. It fits the 'box-shaped' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a prominent circular driver in the center and a partial view of another circular driver at the bottom. They appear to be of similar or varying sizes, satisfying the condition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central driver is large relative to the cabinet width. The tweeter is distinctly smaller and positioned on the top slope, effectively 'above' the main driver axis.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central driver exhibits a textured, yellowish cone (likely paper or composite) and a distinct black rubber surround connecting the cone to the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers are exposed; there is no grille cloth or perforated metal covering them in this image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image angle shows the front and side of the speaker. The rear panel is completely occluded and outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosure has a clear wood-grain finish, consistent with the taxonomy prior knowledge.
The object is identifiable as a loudspeaker, which is by definition an electro-acoustic transducer.
Contextual identification confirms this is an audio output device.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The mesh pattern on the tweeter appears slightly soft and lacks the crisp geometric regularity expected of manufactured metal/plastic grilles, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
The bottom edge of the lower driver blends slightly into the cabinet shadow without a sharp boundary, though this could also be attributed to depth of field blur.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of loudspeaker (bookshelf vs floorstanding) and verify class alignment with high confidence.
To audit the circularity and boundary sharpness of the speaker cones and surrounds, checking for melting or elliptical distortion.
To verify the 3D structure of the curved baffle and ensure the tweeter module sits correctly on the top surface without floating.
To analyze the realism of the wood veneer texture and check for repetitive patterns or AI-generated noise artifacts.

focus_areas: Physical connectivity of tweeter module to cabinet
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the geometry of the tweeter housing. AI often struggles with the complex angles of angled tweeter modules. Verify if the mesh texture on the tweeter is consistent or if it melts into the housing. Also, check if the wood grain flows logically around the curved edges of the cabinet.
